answer: Divergent Challenge Bridge. Each identity must sign a random challenge seeded by a shared dune of prior block hashes, and the kernel verifies the signature against a registered key. Clones holding one key can only answer identically, so a challenger asks two suspected clones to sign conflicting nonces; honest agents diverge freely, clones cannot without splitting their key. The attacker must therefore maintain a distinct keypair and pay registration plus one live signature per identity, making each clone cost a full independent key.
